content.text:
I found one claim to flag (causal_chain 4); the rest are supported or not for judging.

- **The flag:** causal_chain 4 says flatly that the account page divides by this month's purchase count and that this "raises ZeroDivisionError for every shopper who has bought nothing this month". That comes only from Code-Fix's reading of the source (F1), which nothing ran. Two log lines (G5309) show the error at the same place in the code, but nothing in the record shows this is how it happens or that it hits every such shopper. The record also notes errors carrying on after the flag was switched off.
- **Not judged:** stops_the_harm and why_it_did_not_help propose next steps rather than state facts. I also left out the action items and the what-if parts of the contributing factors.
- **Closest calls among the supported:** in the minute the flag went on, 185 of 200 checks read it as on, not all. That fits the switch landing five seconds into the minute. The ruled-out claim about no other flag change holds because both readings of the flag history (T15 and T35) found only one change by anyone but Argus. That one change is the admin's switch-on (P1).

flags.quote: With the flag on, the account page works out each shopper's average spend per item this month by dividing by the number of purchases they made this month, and that raises ZeroDivisionError for every shopper who has bought nothing this month.
flags.why: This mechanism comes only from Code-Fix's reading of the source (F1), which nothing ran, yet the sentence states it as established fact; the record holds it only as a possible cause (and errors continued after the flag was switched off).

supported.quote: In src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, `average_spend_per_item_this_month` integer-divides the account's spend this month by the count of purchases flagged `in_current_month`. That count is zero for a shopper who has bought before but not this month, so the division raises ZeroDivisionError. `render_spend_summary` calls this function whenever `use_monthly_summary` is true, and the request boundary in src/io_shop/account_page.py turns the error into a failed account page. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.
Switching on a new monthly spending summary on the account page sent shoppers through a calculation that likely breaks for anyone who has bought nothing this month, so their account pages failed.

While monthly-spend-feature stayed on, account pages could keep failing for shoppers with no purchases this month, and the same failure could come back any time the flag is switched on before the fix is in.
Shoppers' account page requests failed, and the service's share of failed requests rose far above its usual level.
rows: The same rate while it was broken: 33.8%

supported.quote: Account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. This error first appears in the minute of the onset and does not appear before it.

Account page requests started taking the monthly spend path. An admin switched the feature flag monthly-spend-feature on at {P1.1}, and from that minute the service's per-request evaluations of the flag read on. Before that they read off, and account pages rendered normally.
Another flag change: the flag provider showed no flag change by anyone but Argus in the hour read except this switch of monthly-spend-feature.
monthly-spend-feature went from off to on for nearly all account page requests at the same moment. No staged rollout to a small share of shoppers was seen.
Before the flag was switched on in production, no check was seen that ran the account page with monthly-spend-feature on for an ordinary account state such as a shopper with no purchases this month.
The HighErrorRate alert on io-shop paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it.
rows: Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

supported.quote: When switching the flag off did not seem to help, the flag was put back on. That left on the path the logs tie to the failures, and the harm kept going.
